clue.text: Feeling very self-conscious in say, Arab country, returning first-class

parts.note: say introduces an example, and 'for example' is abbreviated e.g.
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

indicators.note: returning suggests coming back the other way, so the letters standing for first-class are read from right to left

parts.note: A1 means first-class, and crosswords write the figure 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: A traveller feels awkward and exposed flying home from an Arab state in the posh seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'self-conscious' usually means shy; here it is read literally, as being conscious of little but oneself. 'returning' turns only AI, making IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical literal reading: an obsessive preoccupation with oneself is being conscious of self to an extreme degree, not the shyness the phrase normally means.

clue.text: Sense approval amongst the crew

indicators.note: amongst says the word of approval sits surrounded by the letters of the crew

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight rowers, as in the Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race
yes is the word that gives approval

explanation.surface: A captain picks up a feeling of agreement among the ship's company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sense' reads as a verb, to detect a mood, but it is a noun: one of the five senses. 'amongst' makes the crew, a rowing one, the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Example of the category: vision is one of the five faculties, alongside hearing, smell, taste and touch.

clue.text: Take power from wizard's fur

indicators.note: take is the instruction to remove something: here the letter standing for power
from names what the letter is removed out of: the wizard's surname

parts.note: Harry Potter is the boy wizard of J.K. Rowling's novels
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone drains the magic from a sorcerer's fur cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' and 'from' remove P from POTTER. The fur is the animal's pelt, once used for coats and collars.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary sense: the word names not only the river animal but also its dense brown pelt, once prized by furriers.

clue.text: How KLM are organised?

parts.note: the surface asks about the Dutch airline's corporate structure; read KLM instead as three separate letters and ask what puts them in that sequence

explanation.walkthrough: There is no wordplay to assemble. KLM is the Dutch national airline, and the capitals invite you to think of its management, not of K, L and M as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: K, L and M are consecutive in the ABC, so they are arranged in dictionary order.

clue.text: Trendy set's contribution

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in crowd
to set something down is to put it there; the 's is only the surface's possessive

explanation.surface: The fashionable crowd has chipped in with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' reads as a noun, the fashionable crowd, but it is the verb meaning to place.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: what you add to a discussion or project, as in thanking a colleague for their ideas and suggestions.

clue.text: Hold on — complaint's not finished!

indicators.note: not finished says the word for a complaint is cut short, stopping one letter before its end

parts.note: a gripe is a grumble or minor complaint; the 's is only the surface's 'is'
the last letter of the complaint word, the one that goes missing

explanation.surface: A caller is told to wait because there is more grumbling still to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold on' reads as a request to wait, but it means keep a firm grasp. 'not finished' drops the last letter of GRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to hold on to something is to keep a firm grasp of it, as when clinging tight to a rail.

clue.text: Duck and oranges do mix well together

indicators.note: mix well together is a recipe instruction to stir things up, so the letters of the two words before it are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook observes that duck goes nicely with oranges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix well together' rearranges ORANGES DO. The surface is the classic dish duck à l'orange; 'and' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example of the category: it is a large fish-eating diving bird of rivers and lakes, one of the sawbills.

clue.text: Heartless vet's a loathsome creature

indicators.note: heartless says the word for vet loses its heart, the single letter at its very centre

parts.note: to vet something is to inspect it closely, as when checking a candidate's background
the middle letter of the seven, the one that goes missing

explanation.surface: A cruel animal doctor is a truly horrible person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vet' looks like an animal doctor but is the verb meaning to check. 'Heartless' removes the middle letter, P, of INSPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose, opinionated description: many people find bugs and creepy-crawlies revolting, and the word is also an insult for a contemptible person.

clue.text: Dishy bloke providing brief about new church before tea

indicators.note: about says the word for providing a brief goes round the three short pieces that follow it

parts.note: priming someone is briefing them, giving them the facts they need in advance

indicators.note: before fixes the order inside: new and church come ahead of the word for tea

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new, as in NT for New Testament
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England
char is British slang for tea, from the Chinese cha

explanation.surface: A good-looking man hands over notes on the new church just ahead of the afternoon break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'providing brief' is one unit, a verb meaning briefing, not 'providing' plus a short word. 'about' makes it the container, and 'before' puts new and church ahead of tea inside.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a handsome man: the fairy-tale hero who wins Cinderella is the byword for an ideal, attractive suitor.

clue.text: One leaves editor struggling with pressure put on tabloid

indicators.note: put on says the letter for pressure is added to the end of what the rest has built
struggling suggests something thrashing about in disorder, so what is left of the editor is put in a new order
leaves says the letter standing for one departs from the word editor

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A departure leaves a newspaper editor battling the strain their paper is under.
explanation.walkthrough: A red top is a British tabloid with a red masthead, like The Sun or the Mirror. 'leaves' takes I from EDITOR, 'struggling' turns EDTOR into REDTO, and 'put on' adds P.
explanation.definitionFit: British press slang: mass-market tabloids such as The Sun and the Daily Mirror print their mastheads in red, hence the nickname.

clue.text: Mammal meat — there's a kilo out on balance

indicators.note: out says the letter for a kilo is taken away from the word for meat

parts.note: pork is the meat of a pig
K is the abbreviation for kilo, as in kg
poise is balance, a steady and graceful bearing

explanation.surface: A butcher checking a meat order finds the weight is a kilo off, all things considered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes the K from PORK, leaving POR. The phrase 'on balance' looks like the idiom for 'all things considered', but balance alone is a noun meaning steadiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Example of the category: this small toothed whale, a relative of the dolphin, breathes air and suckles its young.

clue.text: Doctor who finally enters after international designer

indicators.note: enters says the last letter of who goes inside the abbreviation for doctor, along with the letter it follows
after fixes the order inside: the letter taken from who comes behind the one for international

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for international, as in IMF

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word who

explanation.surface: The Time Lord at last walks in, following a fashion designer of world renown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor who' reads as Doctor Who, the BBC's time-travelling hero, but the words split: 'finally' takes the O of who, 'enters' puts it inside DR, and 'after' places it behind the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by name: Christian Dior was the French couturier who founded his fashion house in 1946 and launched the New Look.

clue.text: Presence of minister with bad acne

parts.note: as a verb, to minister to someone is to attend them, as a nurse does a patient

indicators.note: bad describes the acne as being in a poor state, so its four letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A member of the clergy turns up with a nasty outbreak of spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' looks like a clergyman or politician but is the verb meaning to tend. 'bad' rearranges ACNE into ANCE; 'of' and 'with' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both name the fact of being there, as when a register records who has turned up.

clue.text: Being tortured heretics fled town

indicators.note: being tortured suggests something twisted and racked out of shape, so the letters of the two words that follow are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Under torture, religious dissenters escaped from the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being tortured' rearranges HERETICS FLED. The town is in Derbyshire, in the English Midlands, and is known for the crooked spire of its church.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by name: it is a market town in Derbyshire in the English Midlands, famous for its church's twisted spire.

clue.text: If it's low you may get depression or tension when worried

definitions.text: If it's low you may get depression
definitions.note: a descriptive clause, not a noun: 'it' stands for the answer, a substance whose shortage is linked to low mood

indicators.note: worried describes something agitated and shaken up, so the letters of the two words just before it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: When some level drops, an anxious person can end up gloomy or stressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description in which 'it' is the answer. 'when worried' rearranges OR TENSION; 'depression' belongs to the definition, not the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: this brain chemical, a neurotransmitter, helps regulate mood, and a shortage of it has long been linked to feeling depressed.

clue.text: Charge for iron's expensive at first

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, from the Latin ferrum

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word expensive

explanation.surface: The price of an iron starts out steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron' looks like the household appliance but is the metal, with its chemical symbol. 'for' joins the definition to the wordplay; 'at first' takes one letter of 'expensive'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sum of money asked for a service, such as what a lawyer or agent bills you.

clue.text: Saying rude things about old blood sport

indicators.note: about says the word for saying rude things goes round the letter for old

parts.note: cursing is swearing, using foul language
O is the abbreviation for old, as in OT for Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone is being foul-mouthed about a traditional hunting pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but wraps CURSING round O. The sport is chasing hares with greyhounds, now banned in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Example of the category: it is the pursuit of hares by greyhounds hunting by sight, an activity in which an animal is killed.

clue.text: Expose loft and cause a massive disturbance?

definitions.meaning: taken literally: lifting the top off a house would leave its attic open to the sky
the idiom for making a tremendous din, as a cheering or furious crowd does

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a literal picture, not a dictionary meaning, which the question mark admits; 'and' simply joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom read two ways: literally, lifting off a building's top would uncover the attic; figuratively, it means making a deafening noise or furious fuss.

clue.text: Bloomer made by silly 10 hugging companion

indicators.note: hugging says the rearranged letters wrap their arms round the abbreviation for companion
silly describes something scatty and disordered, so the letters of the answer at 10 are put in a new order

parts.note: a cross-reference: use the answer to 10 across, the fashion designer DIOR
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British order of merit

explanation.surface: A foolish ten-year-old makes a blunder while cuddling a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, but here it is something that blooms. '10' means the answer to 10 across, which 'silly' rearranges to ORID before 'hugging' wraps it round the companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful description: a bloomer is anything that blooms, and this is a showy flowering plant prized by collectors.

clue.text: For a tower, draughtsman may use this

definitions.note: a descriptive clause, not a noun: 'this' stands for the answer, an instrument found in a drawing office

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in weighing the pros and cons
read it as tow-er, something that tows: a tractor pulls trailers and ploughs behind it

explanation.surface: Someone designing a tall building is told which instrument the drawing office would reach for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' looks like a tall building, the sort of thing a draughtsman draws, but it is to be read as tow-er: a vehicle that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: it is the semicircular drawing instrument for measuring and marking angles, a staple of any technical drawing kit.

clue.text: Bones starts to run as spock is taken ill

indicators.note: ill describes something out of sorts, so the five initial letters are put in a new order
starts to asks for the opening letter of each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: The Enterprise's doctor breaks into a run as the Vulcan first officer falls sick.
explanation.walkthrough: In Star Trek, Bones is the nickname of Dr McCoy, Spock's shipmate; here it is literal. 'starts to' gives RASIT, which 'ill' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomical example: each tarsus is the cluster of small ankle bones at the back of the foot, and this is the Latin plural.

clue.text: Perhaps rosemary's in another bed

indicators.note: in says the letters wanted lie inside the two words that follow, in order, running across the space between them

explanation.surface: Rosemary, it seems, has been moved to a different bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is' and 'in' marks the hiding place. 'Perhaps' warns that rosemary is only an example of what is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: rosemary is one of the aromatic culinary plants of the kitchen garden, and 'perhaps' flags that it is only one instance.

clue.text: Old doctor drops boxes — one's very heavy!

definitions.note: read as 'one that is very heavy': a description of the animal wanted, not a straight synonym

indicators.note: drops says the old doctor's name lets go of the letters meaning boxes, which fall off its end

parts.note: Hippocrates was the ancient Greek physician after whom the doctors' oath is named
crates are large wooden boxes for transporting goods

explanation.surface: An elderly physician lets some cartons fall because one of them weighs a ton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks like elderly but means ancient: the Greek physician. 'drops' removes CRATES from HIPPOCRATES, and 'one' turns out to be an animal, not a box.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive hint, not a synonym: the hippopotamus is among the weightiest land animals, an adult tipping the scales at well over a tonne.

clue.text: Conservative has to manage radical writer

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, as in election results
to manage a tricky situation is to handle it
R is the chemist's symbol for a radical, a group of atoms, in a formula

explanation.surface: A right-wing politician is obliged to keep a firebrand author under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' only joins the pieces. The writer is Raymond Chandler, the American crime novelist who created the private eye Philip Marlowe.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by surname: Raymond Chandler wrote The Big Sleep and other hard-boiled detective novels featuring Philip Marlowe.

clue.text: Damage caused by couple on motorway when on the way back

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is added to its end, so the word for a couple comes second, behind the motorway's letters
on the way back describes a return journey, so the letters for the motorway are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write its figure 1 as the letter I
a couple is a pair, two of a kind

explanation.surface: A crash was caused by two people on the motorway as they drove home.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'on' sends PAIR to the end. 'when on the way back' turns MI, the M1 motorway from London to Leeds, into IM; 'caused by' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to weaken or harm something, as loud music can harm your hearing.

clue.text: A place to hide port

parts.note: den means a hideout, the lair where an animal or a gang lies low

explanation.surface: Somewhere is needed to stash a bottle of fortified wine out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests stashing a bottle of port wine; the definition is a harbour city, in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by name: it is a harbour city in Yemen on the Gulf of the same name, long a refuelling stop for ships.

clue.text: Being game bolt put medal around Powell's head

parts.note: a bolt is a metal pin that fastens things together

indicators.note: put is the instruction to place the medal word somewhere; the word around then says where
around says the word for a medal goes on either side of the single letter taken from Powell

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or honour

indicators.note: head points to the first letter of Powell, the front of the name

explanation.surface: In a sporting gesture, one sprinter drapes a medal over a rival's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures Jamaican sprinters Usain Bolt and Asafa Powell, with 'Being game' as 'being a good sport'. 'put' and 'around' wrap GONG round P; 'head' takes Powell's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example of the category: it is the informal name for table tennis, played with small bats and a light hollow ball.
